selected_hotel.name: Tsukiji, Chuo City, Tokyo Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from local vendors. Engage with fishmongers and food artisans who have operated stalls for generations, offering an authentic taste of Tokyo's legendary seafood culture.

experiences.name: Odaiba Waterfront Tech & Culture Day
experiences.description: Visit the futuristic Odaiba island on Tokyo Bay, exploring teamLab Borderless digital art museum, the Toyota Mega Web showroom, and the Miraikan National Museum of Emerging Science. Enjoy stunning waterfront views of Rainbow Bridge and the replica Statue of Liberty while immersing yourself in Japan's cutting-edge tech culture.

experiences.name: Asakusa Traditional Culture & Senso-ji Walk
experiences.description: Wander through Tokyo's oldest district, visiting the magnificent Senso-ji Temple, Nakamise shopping street, and traditional craft workshops. Dress in a rented kimono, participate in a matcha tea ceremony, and discover centuries-old artisan shops selling handmade fans, pottery, and lacquerware.

experiences.name: Akihabara Electric Town & Ramen Tasting
experiences.description: Dive deep into Tokyo's legendary electronics and anime hub, exploring multi-floor gadget stores, retro game arcades, and maid cafes. Cap the evening with a guided ramen tasting experience at a local ramen alley, sampling regional styles including tonkotsu, shoyu, and miso broths.

experiences.name: Odaiba Beach Sunset & Yakatabune Dinner Cruise
experiences.description: Relax on Odaiba's artificial sandy beach along Tokyo Bay before boarding a traditional yakatabune wooden boat for a sunset dinner cruise. Enjoy a curated bento-style meal featuring seasonal Japanese dishes while gliding past the illuminated Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo skyline, blending beachfront relaxation with authentic local cuisine.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo, Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Tsukiji, Chuo City, Tokyo Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Narita Express (N'EX) or Limousine Bus to central Tokyo. Budget tip: use the N'EX + Suica card combo deal (~¥3,500) for convenient travel and a rechargeable IC card for the rest of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into your Tsukiji boutique stay. Once settled, take a short walk to explore the Tsukiji Outer Market (the inner wholesale market relocated to Toyosu, but the outer market is still vibrant). Browse fresh seafood stalls, street snacks, and local vendors. Pick up a tamagoyaki (rolled egg) or fresh scallop on a stick for a light snack (~¥200–500).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to nearby Hamarikyu Gardens (entry ¥300) for a relaxing sunset walk among traditional Japanese gardens beside Tokyo Bay. Afterward, grab a budget-friendly dinner at one of the many ramen or izakaya spots around Tsukiji or Ginza's backstreets.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick onigiri (rice ball) from a 7-Eleven or FamilyMart at the airport (~¥150)
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a light snack at Tsukiji Outer Market on arrival (~¥300–600)
meals.dinner: Ramen at a local Tsukiji-area shop such as a tonkotsu or shoyu ramen joint (~¥800–1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport — essential for all Tokyo transit. Keep receipts for budget tracking. April weather is typically mild (15–20°C), cherry blossoms may still be visible.

day_by_day.morning: Start early at Tsukiji Outer Market for a classic Tokyo breakfast. Try fresh sushi, grilled seafood skewers, and tamagoyaki directly from the stalls. This is one of Tokyo's most authentic food experiences at very low cost (~¥500–1,000 total).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway to Akihabara (Electric Town) — the heart of Tokyo's tech and otaku culture. Explore multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera and BIC Camera, retro game shops, anime merchandise stores, and maid cafés. Window shopping is free; budget a small amount for souvenirs or a used retro game (~¥500–2,000).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the back alleys of Akihabara for dinner. Try a budget curry rice at CoCo Ichibanya or a gyudon (beef bowl) at Yoshinoya or Matsuya (~¥500–700). Then browse the illuminated electronics district at night — it's a spectacular visual experience.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market seafood breakfast — fresh tuna sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled scallops (~¥600–1,000)
meals.lunch: Convenience store lunch (7-Eleven or Lawson) — onigiri, sandwiches, hot foods (~¥400–600)
meals.dinner: Gyudon beef bowl at Yoshinoya or Matsuya in Akihabara (~¥500–700)

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored on foot. Many electronics stores have tax-free counters for tourists — bring your passport. Free Wi-Fi available in most stores.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa (free entry) — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic temple. Arrive early to avoid crowds. Walk through Nakamise Shopping Street for traditional souvenirs and snacks like ningyo-yaki (doll-shaped cakes) and senbei rice crackers (~¥100–300 each).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center (free, great views from the top floor observation deck). Walk along the Sumida River toward Tokyo Skytree — you can admire it from outside for free, or splurge on the observation deck (¥2,100 for the lower deck). Alternatively, save money and enjoy the exterior and surrounding Solamachi mall.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Asakusa's Hoppy Street (Hoppy Dori) — a retro alley filled with casual izakayas serving yakitori, oden, and cheap draft beer or hoppy drinks. Very local atmosphere, very affordable (~¥1,000–1,500 including drinks).

meals.breakfast: Ningyo-yaki and green tea from Nakamise Street stalls (~¥300–500)
meals.lunch: Tempura tendon at a local Asakusa restaurant — look for lunch set menus (~¥800–1,200)
meals.dinner: Izakaya on Hoppy Street — yakitori skewers, oden, draft beer (~¥1,000–1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free but very busy by midday — go early. Asakusa is very walkable from Tsukiji via the Oedo or Asakusa subway line (~¥200). April cherry blossoms may still linger along the Sumida River.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Ueno Park (free entry) — a massive public park home to several world-class museums. Visit the Tokyo National Museum (¥1,000) for an introduction to Japanese art, history, and culture, including samurai armor, ukiyo-e prints, and ancient artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ueno's Ameyoko Market — a lively outdoor market street with vendors selling fresh seafood, dried goods, clothing, and street food. Great for budget shopping and snacking. Try takoyaki (octopus balls) or yakitori (~¥300–600). Then walk to nearby Yanaka, one of Tokyo's best-preserved old neighborhoods, for a nostalgic stroll through traditional shitamachi streets.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Yanaka Ginza — a charming old shopping street with budget-friendly local eateries. Try menchi-katsu (fried meat patty) from a butcher shop or sit down at a cozy soba restaurant (~¥600–1,000).

meals.breakfast: Coffee and toast at a retro kissaten (old-school coffee shop) near Ueno (~¥400–600)
meals.lunch: Street food at Ameyoko Market — takoyaki, grilled skewers, fresh fruit (~¥500–800)
meals.dinner: Soba or udon at a local Yanaka restaurant (~¥600–1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Ueno Park is a short subway ride from Tsukiji. On weekends, Ameyoko is especially lively. Yanaka is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Harajuku. Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine (free entry) — a serene forested Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji. A peaceful contrast to the busy city. Walk through the wooded approach path and observe traditional rituals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Takeshita Street in Harajuku — Tokyo's famous youth fashion hub. Browse quirky fashion boutiques, costume shops, and unique street food like crepes and cotton candy (~¥400–700 for a crepe). Then head to Omotesando for window shopping along Tokyo's most stylish boulevard — free to walk and observe.
day_by_day.evening: Take the Yamanote Line to Shibuya. Witness the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing at dusk — one of the world's busiest pedestrian crossings and a must-see spectacle. Grab dinner at a budget ramen or sushi chain in the Shibuya area.

meals.breakfast: Onigiri and coffee from a convenience store near your hotel (~¥300–500)
meals.lunch: Harajuku crepe from a street stall + convenience store snacks (~¥400–700)
meals.dinner: Standing sushi bar (kaiten-zushi or tachinomi sushi) in Shibuya (~¥800–1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is free. Takeshita Street is pedestrian-only and very crowded on weekends — go early afternoon. Shibuya Crossing is best experienced from street level or from the Starbucks window above (buy a coffee to stay).

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shinjuku — start with a free visit to the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (free, open from 9:00 AM) for panoramic 360-degree views of Tokyo including Mt. Fuji on clear days. One of the best free views in the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500 entry) — one of Tokyo's most beautiful parks, especially stunning in cherry blossom season. Enjoy a peaceful picnic lunch on the lawns. Afterward, explore the Shinjuku underground shopping arcades and the electronics/camera shops around Yodobashi Akiba.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the narrow alleyways of Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) in Shinjuku — a tiny alley packed with tiny yakitori bars serving grilled chicken skewers, offal, and cold beer. Very atmospheric and budget-friendly (~¥1,000–1,500 for food and a drink). Then walk through Kabukicho entertainment district for a visual spectacle.

meals.breakfast: Morning set at a Denny's Japan or Jonathan's family restaurant (~¥500–700) — Japanese breakfast sets are great value
meals.lunch: Picnic in Shinjuku Gyoen — buy bento boxes from a nearby convenience store (~¥500–700)
meals.dinner: Yakitori skewers and beer at Omoide Yokocho (~¥1,000–1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is free — north tower is open until 10:30 PM. Shinjuku Gyoen does not allow alcohol. Omoide Yokocho is cash-only at most stalls.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island. Take the driverless Yurikamome monorail (scenic ride, ~¥320) from Shimbashi. Visit teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets digital art museum (book in advance, ~¥3,200) — an unmissable immersive tech-art experience perfectly aligned with tech culture interests.
day_by_day.afternoon: After teamLab, explore the free areas of Odaiba: the life-size Gundam statue (free), DiverCity Tokyo Plaza shopping mall, and the waterfront promenade with views of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline. Visit the free Fuji TV building exterior or the Toyota Mega Web (free car museum).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the mainland via the scenic Rainbow Bridge walk (free, weather permitting) or monorail. Dinner in the Shimbashi area — a salaryman's district with cheap izakayas and ramen shops serving great value set meals.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast before departure (~¥300–500)
meals.lunch: Food court in DiverCity Tokyo Plaza or a ramen shop in Odaiba (~¥700–1,000)
meals.dinner: Izakaya set meal in Shimbashi — beer, edamame, yakitori, and rice (~¥1,000–1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Book teamLab tickets online in advance — they often sell out. The Yurikamome monorail offers stunning views of Tokyo Bay. Odaiba is very walkable once you arrive.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Toyosu Market (the relocated Tuna Auction site) — book a free tuna auction viewing in advance via the Tokyo Metropolitan Central Wholesale Market website (limited spots, must book ahead). Alternatively, visit the market observation decks for free and see the massive fish market in action.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to central Tokyo and visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum in Ryogoku (¥600) — an outstanding museum showcasing Tokyo's history from the Edo period to modern times, with life-size reconstructions of old neighborhoods, kabuki theaters, and traditional crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to Ryogoku Kokugikan (Sumo Arena) to see the exterior and visit the free Sumo Museum (free entry during non-tournament periods). Explore the chanko-nabe restaurants in the area — chanko-nabe is the hearty hot pot stew eaten by sumo wrestlers, available at very reasonable prices (~¥1,000–1,500).

meals.breakfast: Fresh sushi or seafood breakfast at Toyosu Market restaurants (~¥800–1,500) — a splurge-worthy experience
meals.lunch: Convenience store or budget teishoku (set meal) near Ryogoku (~¥600–900)
meals.dinner: Chanko-nabe hot pot at a Ryogoku sumo restaurant (~¥1,000–1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Tuna auction viewing at Toyosu must be booked months in advance — check availability before the trip. The Edo-Tokyo Museum is one of the best value museums in Tokyo. Ryogoku is the sumo district — look for sumo wrestlers in the streets.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Jimbocho — Tokyo's famous book town. Dozens of secondhand bookstores line the streets, selling rare books, vintage manga, old maps, and ukiyo-e prints. Even if you don't buy, it's a fascinating cultural neighborhood. Browse Kitazawa Bookstore or Ohya Shobo for vintage prints.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Kanda Myojin Shrine (free) — one of Tokyo's oldest shrines, closely associated with tech culture (many IT companies including game developers come here for blessings). Then head to the nearby Akihabara area for a second tech culture deep dive — explore retro game shops, Gundam model stores, and the Super Potato retro gaming shop.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the free observation deck at Kitte Marunouchi rooftop garden (free) near Tokyo Station for views of the iconic station building. Then explore the Tokyo Station area's underground ramen street (Ramen Street in Tokyo Station's B1 level) for dinner — choose from 8 famous ramen shops (~¥800–1,200).

meals.breakfast: Kissaten (traditional coffee shop) morning set near Jimbocho — toast, boiled egg, coffee (~¥400–600)
meals.lunch: Curry rice at a local Jimbocho curry restaurant — the area is famous for curry (~¥700–1,000)
meals.dinner: Ramen at Tokyo Station's First Avenue Ramen Street (~¥800–1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Jimbocho is a short walk or subway ride from Tsukiji. Kanda Myojin has a fascinating connection to Tokyo's tech industry — many gaming companies have their ema (votive plaques) here. Tokyo Station itself is worth exploring.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Nikko (approximately 2 hours from Tokyo via Tobu Nikko Line — budget option ~¥1,400 one way). Visit the spectacular Toshogu Shrine complex — a UNESCO World Heritage site with ornate mausoleums, pagodas, and the famous 'hear no evil, see no evil, speak no evil' monkey carvings (entry ~¥1,300).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko's Rinno-ji Temple and Futarasan Shrine (combo ticket available). Walk to Shinkyo Bridge — a sacred red lacquered bridge over the Daiya River (viewing from outside is free). Enjoy the mountain scenery and fresh air.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Grab a quick and satisfying dinner near Tsukiji — try a local izakaya or a budget sushi conveyor belt restaurant (kaiten-zushi) where plates start at ¥110 each.

meals.breakfast: Onigiri and coffee from convenience store before departure (~¥300–500)
meals.lunch: Bento box packed from a convenience store or buy yuba (tofu skin) dishes in Nikko — local specialty (~¥500–800)
meals.dinner: Kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) near Tsukiji (~¥800–1,500 for a satisfying meal)

day_by_day.notes: The Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa Station is the budget option to Nikko. Buy a Nikko World Heritage Area Pass for combined entry savings. Nikko can be cold — bring a light jacket. Book the day trip on a weekday to avoid weekend crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Nezu Shrine (free) in Yanaka/Bunkyo area — famous for its hundreds of torii gates (similar to Kyoto's Fushimi Inari but far less crowded). Walk through the tunnel of vermillion gates and explore the peaceful grounds. Then visit the adjacent Nezu Museum (¥1,300) for a superb collection of Asian art in a beautiful garden setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Shibuya's tech district — visit the Google Japan office area or explore the startup hub around Shibuya Stream. Then visit the free Shibuya Sky observation deck... or save money and go to the free rooftop of Shibuya Hikarie or the Scramble Square building exterior. Browse Shibuya's 109 building (free to enter) and Tower Records for music culture.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Tokyo nightlife on a budget — visit a standing bar (tachinomi) in Shibuya or Shinjuku. Many offer drinks from ¥300–500. Alternatively, join a free walking tour or explore the neon-lit streets of Shinjuku's Golden Gai — a maze of tiny bars with cover charges (~¥500–1,000) but very authentic.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near Nezu Shrine — toast and coffee at a local café (~¥400–600)
meals.lunch: Lunch set at a local Yanaka or Sendagi neighborhood restaurant (~¥700–1,000)
meals.dinner: Standing bar snacks and drinks in Shibuya or Golden Gai, Shinjuku (~¥800–1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Nezu Shrine is free and much less crowded than Fushimi Inari in Kyoto. Golden Gai bars are tiny (some seat only 5–6 people) — be respectful and check for cover charges before entering.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mori Art Museum in Roppongi Hills (¥2,000 — includes city observation from Mori Tower) — one of Tokyo's top contemporary art museums with rotating international exhibitions. The Tokyo City View observation deck offers stunning 360-degree views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the National Art Center Tokyo in Roppongi (free entry to the building, exhibition fees vary ~¥1,000–1,500) — a stunning architecturally designed museum with rotating world-class exhibitions. Afterward, walk through Roppongi's art triangle and visit the free outdoor sculptures.
day_by_day.evening: Final special dinner — treat yourself to a slightly elevated but still budget-conscious experience. Visit a conveyor belt sushi restaurant like Sushiro or Kura Sushi (plates from ¥110) or try a shabu-shabu or sukiyaki all-you-can-eat lunch deal at a chain restaurant (~¥1,500–2,000). End the evening with a walk along the illuminated Ginza shopping district — free to stroll and window shop.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area café or convenience store — yogurt, fruit, coffee (~¥400–600)
meals.lunch: Roppongi Hills food court or a nearby ramen shop (~¥700–1,000)
meals.dinner: Conveyor belt sushi at Sushiro or Kura Sushi — budget splurge farewell meal (~¥1,500–2,500)

day_by_day.notes: The Mori Art Museum ticket includes the observation deck — good value. Roppongi is Tokyo's arts district with three major museums in walking distance. Ginza is very walkable from Tsukiji — about 15 minutes on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — return to Tsukiji Outer Market for a farewell breakfast and last-minute souvenir shopping. Pick up high-quality kitchen knives (Tsukiji is famous for them), dried seaweed, wasabi, and Japanese condiments as gifts. Browse the stalls one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, visit any missed spots nearby — Hama-rikyu Gardens for a final peaceful stroll (¥300), or explore the Ginza backstreets for last-minute shopping at 100-yen shops (Daiso) for affordable Japanese souvenirs. Head to the airport via N'EX or Limousine Bus with plenty of time.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — arrive at airport at least 3 hours before international flight. Use remaining Suica card balance at airport convenience stores or vending machines. You can refund the remaining Suica deposit (¥500) at a station service counter.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market farewell feast — fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, miso soup (~¥800–1,200)
meals.lunch: Airport terminal food — ramen or soba at the airport (~¥800–1,200)
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Keep ¥3,000–5,000 in cash for airport transport and final meals. Refund your Suica card at the airport or keep it for a future Japan visit (valid for 10 years). Check airline baggage weight limits before souvenir shopping. Allow extra time for airport security and check-in on departure day.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo, Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Tsukiji, Chuo City, Tokyo Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Narita Express or Limousine Bus to Tsukiji area. Check in to your boutique stay in Tsukiji, Chuo City.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely first walk through the Tsukiji Outer Market (场外市場). Browse the fresh seafood stalls, street snacks, and kitchen tool shops. Pick up tamagoyaki (Japanese rolled omelette) and fresh fruit skewers as a welcome snack. Get oriented with your neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to nearby Hamarikyu Gardens for a peaceful late-afternoon walk along the waterfront (open until 17:00, so aim to arrive by 16:00). Afterward, head back to Tsukiji for a relaxed dinner at one of the market-adjacent sushi restaurants.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or on arrival; alternatively, snack at Tsukiji Outer Market on arrival (try grilled scallops or tuna skewers, ~¥500–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Sushi Zanmai or Daiwa Sushi in Tsukiji — fresh omakase sets at mid-range price (~¥2,500–¥4,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light to recover from jet lag. Stay hydrated and avoid over-scheduling. Purchase a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless transit throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Tsukiji Outer Market for a classic Tokyo breakfast experience — fresh sashimi, tamago, and miso soup. Then walk or take a short metro ride to Ginza for a morning stroll through Japan's most upscale shopping district. Window-shop the flagship stores and admire the architecture of the Sony Building area and Itoya stationery store.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the teamLab Planets TOKYO in Toyosu (short ride from Tsukiji) — an immersive digital art experience that blends tech culture and art beautifully. Book tickets in advance online (~¥3,200 per person). Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the installations.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Toyosu Market's viewing deck (free) to watch the evening operations of Japan's largest wholesale fish market. Then head back toward Ginza or Tsukiji for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast set — fresh sashimi don (tuna rice bowl) at Nakaya or similar stall (~¥1,200–¥1,800)
meals.lunch: Ramen at a local shop near teamLab Planets in Toyosu (~¥900–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: Tempura Kondo or a mid-range tempura restaurant in Ginza (~¥3,000–¥5,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Planets tickets sell out fast — book at least 2–3 weeks in advance at teamlab.art. Wear comfortable socks as shoes are removed inside.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Asakusa — Tokyo's most traditional district. Visit Senso-ji Temple early morning when crowds are thinner. Walk the Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional souvenirs, ningyo-yaki cakes, and crafts. Explore the surrounding Asakusa streets for old Edo-era atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Edo-Tokyo Museum in Ryogoku (short ride from Asakusa) — a world-class museum showcasing Tokyo's history from the Edo period to modern times (~¥600 entry). Alternatively, explore the Sumida Hokusai Museum for Japanese woodblock print culture (~¥400).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Akihabara (Electric Town) — Tokyo's iconic tech and pop culture hub. Explore multi-floor electronics shops like Yodobashi Camera, retro game stores, anime merchandise shops, and maid cafés. This is a must for tech culture enthusiasts.

meals.breakfast: Café Combini breakfast or Asakusa's Pelican Café for toast and coffee (~¥600–¥900)
meals.lunch: Monja-yaki (Tokyo-style savory pancake) in Asakusa's Monja Street (~¥1,500–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Akihabara — try a themed restaurant or grab a hearty meal at a gyudon (beef bowl) chain like Yoshinoya or Sukiya, or visit a local izakaya (~¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter. April is cherry blossom season — Sumida Park near Asakusa is one of Tokyo's top hanami (flower viewing) spots. Check bloom status and bring a picnic blanket if blossoms are still out.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ueno Park — a sprawling cultural hub. In April, the park may still have cherry blossoms. Explore the Tokyo National Museum (Japan's largest museum, ~¥1,000) for samurai armor, ancient pottery, ukiyo-e prints, and cultural artifacts. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Ueno's Ameyoko Market — a bustling open-air street market with food, clothes, and goods at bargain prices. Then take the metro to Yanaka, one of Tokyo's best-preserved old neighborhoods. Wander the Yanaka Ginza shotengai (shopping street) and explore the serene Yanaka Cemetery.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shinjuku for the evening. Visit the observation deck of the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building (free, open until 22:30 on most nights) for a panoramic night view of Tokyo. Then explore Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — a narrow alley of tiny yakitori stalls.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area café or convenience store breakfast (~¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Ameyoko Market street food — try fresh seafood, gyoza, or skewers (~¥800–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Yakitori and beer at Omoide Yokocho, Shinjuku (~¥2,000–¥3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Saturdays in Shinjuku are lively — arrive at Omoide Yokocho before 19:00 to secure a spot at a stall. The Government Building observation deck is free and offers one of the best night views in Tokyo.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Harajuku. Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine — a serene forested Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji. Walk the forested gravel path and participate in a traditional prayer ritual. Then explore Yoyogi Park, which is especially beautiful in spring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Takeshita Street in Harajuku for quirky fashion, crepes, and youth pop culture. Then head to Omotesando — Tokyo's 'Champs-Élysées' — for upscale boutiques and stunning architecture (Prada building, Omotesando Hills). Visit the Omotesando Hills complex designed by Tadao Ando.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya. Experience the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing at night — one of the world's busiest intersections. Visit Shibuya Sky observation deck (~¥2,000) for stunning rooftop views. Explore Shibuya's trendy bars and restaurants for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Harajuku crepe from Marion Crepes or Angel's Heart (~¥500–¥800) as a morning treat after the shrine visit
meals.lunch: Omotesando — try Afuri ramen (yuzu shio ramen, ~¥1,200) or a café lunch in the Omotesando Hills food level (~¥1,500–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Shibuya — Ichiran Ramen (solo booth ramen experience, ~¥1,000) or a casual izakaya in Dogenzaka (~¥2,000–¥3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free to enter. Sunday mornings at Yoyogi Park often feature street performers and cosplay gatherings — a great cultural snapshot. Book Shibuya Sky tickets online in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island. Visit the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan) — one of Japan's best science and tech museums, featuring ASIMO robots, space exploration exhibits, and AI displays (~¥630). Perfect for tech culture lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the rest of Odaiba: see the life-size Unicorn Gundam statue at DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (free), browse the retro arcade at Joypolis (or just walk the waterfront), and enjoy views of the Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo Bay. Visit teamLab Border (if not already visited) — another immersive digital art space.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo. Head to Roppongi for the evening — visit Roppongi Hills and the Mori Art Museum (open until 22:00, ~¥2,000) featuring contemporary art with a stunning city view from the 52nd floor. Explore Roppongi's international dining and nightlife scene.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) breakfast near hotel — onigiri, tamagoyaki, and green tea (~¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Odaiba — Aqua City or DiverCity food court; try a Japanese curry set or tonkatsu (~¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Roppongi — mid-range Japanese restaurant; try Tofuya Ukai (tofu kaiseki, book ahead, ~¥5,000–¥8,000) or a casual sushi bar (~¥2,500–¥3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan is closed on Tuesdays — Monday is a great day to visit. The Gundam statue is free and very photogenic. Odaiba is accessible via the Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi — a scenic ride in itself.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (about 2 hours from Tokyo by Tobu Nikko Line or Shinkansen). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine — an ornate and elaborately decorated mausoleum complex for Tokugawa Ieyasu. Explore the shrine complex, pagodas, and the famous 'see no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil' monkey carvings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko: walk to Rinno-ji Temple and the Shinkyo Sacred Bridge over the Daiya River. If time allows, take a bus to Kegon Falls — one of Japan's most beautiful waterfalls (~¥570 for elevator). Enjoy the lush mountain scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Have a relaxed dinner near the hotel in Tsukiji or Ginza area to recover from the day trip.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel area or convenience store before departing (~¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Nikko — yuba (tofu skin) cuisine, a local specialty; try a set lunch at a restaurant near the shrine (~¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Back in Tsukiji — a comforting bowl of kaisendon (seafood rice bowl) or soba at a local restaurant (~¥1,200–¥2,000)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Tobu Nikko Pass for unlimited rides and discounts (~¥4,780 from Asakusa). Start early — aim to leave Tokyo by 8:00 AM. Nikko can be chilly in April, so bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Koenji — a bohemian, counter-culture neighborhood known for vintage shops, indie music, and authentic local life. Browse the dozens of secondhand clothing and vinyl record stores along the Koenji shopping arcades. A refreshing contrast to Tokyo's high-tech districts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Nakameguro — especially beautiful in April when cherry blossoms line the Meguro River (check bloom status). Walk the canal-side paths, browse boutique shops, and enjoy the neighborhood's creative café culture. Visit a specialty coffee shop for an afternoon break.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ebisu and Daikanyama — upscale yet relaxed neighborhoods. Visit Daikanyama T-Site (a stunning architectural bookstore and cultural complex) and browse its curated books, music, and café. Enjoy dinner in the area.

meals.breakfast: Koenji local kissaten (traditional Japanese café) — morning set with toast, egg, and coffee (~¥600–¥900)
meals.lunch: Nakameguro — canal-side café lunch or bento from a local deli (~¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Daikanyama or Ebisu — Log Road Daikanyama restaurants or a mid-range Italian/French bistro (~¥2,500–¥4,000)

day_by_day.notes: Nakameguro cherry blossoms (if still blooming) are best experienced in early evening when lanterns light up the canal. Daikanyama T-Site is open until 26:00 (2 AM) — a late-night cultural gem.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Akihabara for a deeper tech culture dive — explore multi-story retro gaming shops like Super Potato, visit the Gundam Café, and check out the Radio Kaikan electronics building. Browse the latest gadgets, components, and collectibles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby 3331 Arts Chiyoda — a community arts center in a converted school building showcasing local artists and tech-art crossovers (free or low-cost entry). Then visit the Intermediatheque museum in the KITTE building near Tokyo Station — a fascinating free museum blending natural history and design.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Tokyo Station area: admire the beautifully restored red-brick Tokyo Station facade, browse the underground Ramen Street (Tokyo Ramen Street in First Avenue Tokyo Station) for dinner, and pick up high-quality omiyage (souvenir sweets) from the Gransta shopping complex.

meals.breakfast: Akihabara area — try a maid café breakfast experience (unique cultural experience, ~¥1,000–¥1,500 with cover charge)
meals.lunch: Kanda — try Kanda Yabu Soba, one of Tokyo's oldest and most respected soba restaurants (~¥1,500–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Tokyo Ramen Street at Tokyo Station — choose from 8 top ramen shops representing different regional styles (~¥900–¥1,300)

day_by_day.notes: Intermediatheque is free and often overlooked by tourists — a hidden gem. Maid café experiences are a quintessential Akihabara activity; prices include a minimum order.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura (about 1 hour from Tokyo by JR Yokosuka Line from Shimbashi). Visit the Great Buddha (Kotoku-in Daibutsu) — a 13.35-meter bronze statue dating to 1252. Explore the surrounding temple grounds and hike the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through the forested hills.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Hasedera Temple — one of Kamakura's most beautiful temples, featuring a 9-meter wooden Kannon statue, a cave network, and stunning hydrangea gardens. Walk along Komachi-dori shopping street for local crafts, matcha sweets, and shirasu (whitebait) dishes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo. Enjoy a Friday evening in the Ginza area — browse the galleries (many open late on Fridays), visit the Ginza Six luxury mall's rooftop garden (free), or enjoy a cocktail at a Ginza bar.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast near hotel before departure (~¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Kamakura — shirasu don (whitebait rice bowl) at a restaurant near Hase Station, a local specialty (~¥1,200–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Ginza — Sukiyabashi Jiro (if budget allows, ~¥30,000+, book months ahead) OR a mid-range sushi bar in the area (~¥3,000–¥5,000)

day_by_day.notes: Kamakura is walkable or accessible by local bus between sites. The JR Pass covers the Yokosuka Line. April weather in Kamakura is pleasant — great for the hiking trail. Arrive early to avoid weekend crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Nezu Museum in Omotesando — a beautiful private museum of Asian art with a stunning bamboo garden (~¥1,300). Then explore the quiet backstreets of Aoyama, known for high-end design studios, architecture, and the Aoyama Cemetery (free, beautiful in spring).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Harajuku's Ura-Harajuku (backstreets) for independent fashion designers and streetwear boutiques. Visit the Design Festa Gallery — a quirky, ever-changing art space run by artists (~¥500 or free depending on exhibition). Then visit Prada Aoyama or the Spiral Building for architectural appreciation.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's beloved bohemian neighborhood. Explore vintage clothing shops, independent theaters, live music venues, and cozy bars. Catch a live music performance at one of the small venues if available.

meals.breakfast: Aoyama — café breakfast at a specialty coffee shop like Omotesando Koffee or Blue Bottle Coffee (~¥700–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Harajuku — Gyukatsu Motomura (beef cutlet restaurant, ~¥1,500) or a café on Cat Street (~¥1,200–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Shimokitazawa — casual curry restaurant (the area is famous for curry shops) or a small izakaya (~¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Shimokitazawa live music venues often have shows starting at 19:00–20:00 with a door charge of ~¥1,500–¥2,500. Check listings at venues like Shelter, Garage, or Club Que.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tsukiji Fish Market area one final time for a proper morning market breakfast — this time try the full experience: fresh uni (sea urchin) on rice, grilled whole scallops, and fresh oysters. Browse the remaining stalls for last-minute food souvenirs (dashi packets, nori, pickles).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sumida Aquarium in Tokyo Skytree Town (~¥2,300) — a beautifully designed aquarium with jellyfish tanks, open-top penguin pool, and interactive exhibits. Then go up Tokyo Skytree — Japan's tallest tower (634m). The Tembo Deck is at 350m (~¥2,100) and Tembo Galleria at 450m (~¥3,400 combined).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Tokyo — return to a favorite neighborhood for a farewell dinner. Consider a kaiseki (traditional multi-course Japanese meal) experience for a special send-off, or revisit a favorite restaurant from the trip.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — full seafood breakfast spread: sashimi, grilled items, tamagoyaki (~¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.lunch: Tokyo Skytree area — Solamachi food hall has excellent options including ramen, donburi, and sweets (~¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Farewell kaiseki dinner at a mid-range kaiseki restaurant in Ginza or Tsukiji (~¥6,000–¥10,000 per person) OR revisit a favorite spot from the trip

day_by_day.notes: Book Tokyo Skytree tickets online in advance, especially for weekends. The Solamachi shopping complex at the base of Skytree is excellent for last-minute souvenirs and food gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo. Enjoy a slow breakfast near the hotel. Do any last-minute packing and souvenir shopping in the Tsukiji or Ginza area. Visit a nearby konbini (convenience store) to pick up Japanese snacks and drinks for the flight home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the boutique stay. Head to the airport via Narita Express from Tokyo Station or Limousine Bus from Ginza. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Enjoy duty-free shopping at Narita — pick up whisky, Kit Kat flavors, or cosmetics.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Japanese breakfast near Tsukiji — miso soup, grilled fish, rice, and pickles at a traditional teishoku restaurant (~¥800–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Airport terminal — Narita has excellent food options including sushi, ramen, and tonkatsu restaurants in the departure hall (~¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Keep transit time generous — Tokyo traffic can be unpredictable. Narita Express takes about 60–80 minutes from Tokyo Station. Return your Suica/Pasmo card at the airport for a refund of the remaining balance (minus a ¥220 handling fee). Declare any food items at customs upon return.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo, Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Tsukiji, Chuo City, Tokyo Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from local vendors. Engage with fishmongers and food artisans who have operated stalls for generations, offering an authentic taste of Tokyo's legendary seafood culture.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tokyo airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange private airport transfer to your boutique stay in Tsukiji, Chuo City.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in and freshen up at your boutique hotel in Tsukiji. Once settled, take a leisurely stroll through the Tsukiji Outer Market to get your bearings — browse the stalls of fresh seafood, pickled vegetables, tamagoyaki shops, and specialty Japanese kitchenware. Grab a light snack to tide you over.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Tokyo with a premium omakase dinner at a renowned sushi counter near Tsukiji. Enjoy a chef-curated multi-course meal featuring the freshest seasonal fish sourced directly from the market. Pair with sake selected by the sommelier.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or at airport
meals.lunch: Light street snacks from Tsukiji Outer Market stalls: fresh uni, tamagoyaki skewers, and matcha soft serve
meals.dinner: Omakase sushi at Sushi Saito annex or a comparable Tsukiji-area Michelin-recognized counter (reservation recommended in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private car or limousine transfer from Narita or Haneda to minimize travel fatigue. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. Keep Day 1 relaxed to combat jet lag. The Tsukiji Outer Market closes most stalls by late afternoon, so a quick browse upon arrival is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for the full Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour experience — sample fresh sushi, grilled scallops, tamagoyaki, pickled plums, and premium dashi broth from legendary vendors. Visit specialist shops for high-grade Japanese knives and ceramics as souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Hamarikyu Gardens (a 10-minute walk from Tsukiji), a stunning Edo-period tidal garden with manicured pine trees and teahouses set against the modern Tokyo skyline. Enjoy a formal matcha tea ceremony at the traditional Nakajima no Ochaya teahouse on the garden's central pond.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the Sumida River by water bus to Asakusa. Explore the lantern-lit Nakamise shopping street leading to Senso-ji Temple, beautifully atmospheric after dark. Dine at a high-end kaiseki restaurant in the Asakusa area showcasing seasonal Japanese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market: fresh tuna sashimi, tamagoyaki, and clam miso soup from market vendors
meals.lunch: Bento box and matcha sweets at Hamarikyu Gardens teahouse
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner at Sometaro or a premium Asakusa ryotei featuring multi-course seasonal Japanese cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is busiest and most vibrant before 9:00 AM. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Book the Hamarikyu matcha ceremony in advance. The water bus from Hamarikyu to Asakusa is a scenic and relaxing way to travel.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Planets digital art museum in Toyosu (15 minutes from Tsukiji by taxi). Immerse yourself in breathtaking large-scale interactive digital installations — a perfect intersection of Japanese art and cutting-edge technology. Book the first entry slot to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the futuristic Toyosu Market observation deck to see Japan's largest wholesale seafood market in action, then head to Odaiba, Tokyo's high-tech waterfront district. Visit the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) to experience ASIMO robots, AI demonstrations, and space exploration exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at a premium restaurant on the upper floors of a Shiodome or Odaiba tower with panoramic views of Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo Bay illuminated at night. Return to Tsukiji by taxi.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a boutique café near Tsukiji serving Japanese-style morning sets (grilled fish, rice, miso soup, pickles)
meals.lunch: Upscale sushi or seafood lunch near Toyosu Market — try a premium chirashi don (scattered sushi bowl) at a market-adjacent restaurant
meals.dinner: Contemporary Japanese cuisine at a bay-view restaurant in Shiodome, such as Nakata Shoten or a comparable high-end venue

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Planets tickets must be booked online well in advance — extremely popular. Allow at least 1.5 hours at teamLab. Miraikan is particularly fascinating for tech enthusiasts. Odaiba is easily accessible via the Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Akihabara, Tokyo's legendary Electric Town, for a deep dive into Japanese tech culture. Explore multi-story electronics megastores (Yodobashi Camera, BIC Camera), retro game shops, and specialist stores for robotics components, rare electronics, and anime merchandise. Visit the Akihabara Radio Kaikan for curated tech and collector culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby 3331 Arts Chiyoda cultural space and then walk to the Kanda Myojin Shrine — one of Tokyo's oldest shrines, interestingly now also a hub for IT company blessings and tech-culture prayer. Continue to the upscale Nihonbashi district for luxury shopping at Coredo Muromachi and a visit to the Mitsukoshi flagship department store's premium food hall (depachika).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a premium teppanyaki dinner in the Ginza district — A5 Wagyu beef prepared tableside by a master chef. After dinner, explore Ginza's illuminated luxury boutiques and art galleries.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby Tsukiji café — Japanese breakfast set with grilled salmon, tamago, rice, and miso
meals.lunch: Akihabara: try a high-quality ramen at a specialist shop (e.g., Fuunji-style tsukemen) or a premium curry at a celebrated Kanda curry house
meals.dinner: A5 Wagyu teppanyaki at Ginza Ukai-tei or Steak Tsukiji Saito — a truly indulgent luxury experience

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best experienced on a weekday morning when it's less crowded. The Kanda Myojin IT blessing is a uniquely Japanese cultural curiosity worth photographing. Ginza is Tokyo's most prestigious shopping district — ideal for an evening stroll.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Yanaka, one of Tokyo's best-preserved historic neighborhoods, for a cultural morning. Wander the atmospheric Yanaka Ginza shopping street, browse antique shops, traditional craft stores, and visit the serene Yanaka Cemetery — famous for its spring cherry blossom trees (possibly still blooming in mid-April). Explore small temples and traditional wooden townhouses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno — Japan's oldest and largest museum, housing an extraordinary collection of samurai armor, ukiyo-e woodblock prints, ancient ceramics, and Buddhist sculptures. Take your time in the main Honkan building and the Japanese Gallery.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at a premium tempura restaurant in Ueno or Ginza — watch master chefs fry seasonal vegetables and seafood to golden perfection in a counter-style setting. Return to Tsukiji by subway.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza street breakfast: fresh-baked melon pan, grilled mochi, and canned coffee from local shops
meals.lunch: Traditional soba lunch at a renowned Yanaka or Nezu soba shop — cold zaru soba with premium dipping sauce
meals.dinner: Premium tempura omakase at Tempura Kondo (Ginza) or Tenichi — a celebrated multi-course tempura experience

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. The Tokyo National Museum requires at least 2-3 hours. Check for any special exhibitions running during your visit. April may still offer late cherry blossom viewing in Yanaka Cemetery.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the upscale Omotesando and Harajuku districts. Visit the iconic Omotesando Hills shopping complex (designed by Tadao Ando) for luxury Japanese and international brands. Walk through the tree-lined Omotesando boulevard and explore the hidden Ura-Harajuku backstreets for cutting-edge Japanese street fashion and design.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Nezu Museum in Omotesando — a world-class private collection of Asian art and antiquities housed in a stunning Kengo Kuma-designed building with a tranquil bamboo garden. Afterward, head to Shibuya to witness the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing from the Scramble Square observation deck (Shibuya Sky) for a bird's-eye view of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Shibuya at a premium yakiniku (Japanese BBQ) restaurant — grill premium A5 Wagyu cuts at your table. Explore the vibrant nightlife of Shibuya's entertainment district afterward.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a premium café in Tsukiji — avocado toast and specialty coffee at a curated local café
meals.lunch: Omotesando: premium lunch at Anniversaire Café or a Michelin-recommended French-Japanese fusion bistro on the boulevard
meals.dinner: Premium yakiniku at Ushigoro Bambina (Shibuya) or comparable A5 Wagyu BBQ restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Omotesando Hills is closed on certain Tuesdays — verify in advance. Nezu Museum is closed on Mondays — consider rescheduling to another day if needed. Shibuya Sky observation deck requires advance ticket booking. The Shibuya Scramble is most impressive at dusk.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (approximately 2 hours by Tobu Limited Express from Asakusa). Explore the UNESCO World Heritage Toshogu Shrine complex — an extraordinarily ornate collection of shrines and mausoleums dedicated to Tokugawa Ieyasu, set in ancient cedar forest. Admire the famous Yomeimon Gate's intricate carvings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko's sacred sites: Futarasan Shrine, Rinnoji Temple, and the serene Shinkyo Sacred Bridge over the Daiya River. Walk through the forested mountain paths surrounding the complex for a deeply atmospheric experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Enjoy a relaxed premium dinner near your Tsukiji hotel — perhaps a high-end shabu-shabu restaurant where you cook premium Wagyu and seasonal vegetables in delicate dashi broth.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Nikko: traditional yuba (tofu skin) cuisine at a local restaurant — Nikko is famous for its yuba dishes, a local specialty
meals.dinner: Premium shabu-shabu at Seryna or a comparable Ginza/Tsukiji area restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Book the Tobu Nikko Limited Express (Spacia) in advance for a comfortable premium ride. The Toshogu complex requires an entrance fee — purchase the combined ticket for all sites. Wear layered clothing as Nikko can be cooler than Tokyo. Return train should be booked by 16:00 to arrive back comfortably.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Shinjuku district, starting with a visit to the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (free entry) for sweeping city views. Walk through the tranquil Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — one of Japan's finest parks, with French formal gardens, English landscape gardens, and a Japanese traditional garden (possible late cherry blossoms).
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive into Shinjuku's tech and gaming culture: visit the Godzilla statue atop Shinjuku Toho Cinema, explore the multi-floor Yodobashi Akiba-style electronics store, and experience the legendary Kabukicho entertainment district in daylight. Visit Robot Restaurant for a pre-dinner cultural spectacle (book in advance).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium Shinjuku kaiseki restaurant or a celebrated French-Japanese fusion restaurant in the Park Hyatt Tokyo (Lost in Translation fame) on the 52nd floor — impeccable food with legendary city views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a Japanese bakery near Tsukiji — fresh cream pan and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Gyoen picnic-style: premium bento box from a Takashimaya Times Square depachika
meals.dinner: New York Grill at Park Hyatt Tokyo (52nd floor) or Kozue Japanese restaurant in the same hotel — both offer extraordinary views and premium menus

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen charges a small entrance fee and prohibits alcohol. Robot Restaurant is a uniquely over-the-top Tokyo experience — more entertainment than dining, so combine with a proper dinner. Park Hyatt restaurant reservations are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mori Art Museum in Roppongi Hills — one of Tokyo's premier contemporary art institutions with rotating exhibitions by leading Japanese and international artists. Combine with the Tokyo City View observation deck on the 52nd floor of Mori Tower for 360-degree panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Roppongi's art triangle: visit the National Art Center Tokyo (largest exhibition space in Japan, with a stunning Kisho Kurokawa-designed undulating glass facade) and the Suntory Museum of Art in Tokyo Midtown. Browse the luxury boutiques and design stores of Tokyo Midtown.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a premium sake tasting dinner at a renowned izakaya in Azabu-Juban (walking distance from Roppongi) — a sophisticated neighborhood izakaya with an extensive sake cellar, pairing seasonal small plates with curated sake flights from across Japan.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a specialty coffee and pastry at a Tsukiji-area artisan café
meals.lunch: Café lunch at the National Art Center's brasserie — Paul Bocuse restaurant within the museum, offering French cuisine in a stunning architectural setting
meals.dinner: Premium izakaya experience at Azabu-Juban — try a multi-course omakase izakaya menu with sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: Check Mori Art Museum exhibition schedule in advance. The museum is open until 22:00 on most days, making it flexible. Roppongi Hills and Tokyo Midtown are connected by a pleasant 10-minute walk. Azabu-Juban is one of Tokyo's most upscale residential neighborhoods with excellent dining.

day_by_day.morning: Take a private guided tour of the Imperial Palace East Gardens — the former site of Edo Castle's innermost circles, now beautifully landscaped public gardens with stone walls, moats, and seasonal flowers. Walk across the iconic Nijubashi Bridge for classic Tokyo photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Marunouchi and Nihonbashi financial districts — Tokyo's historic commercial heart. Visit the Intermediatheque (free entry) in the KITTE building, a fascinating museum of Tokyo University's natural history and scientific collections inside a beautifully restored former post office. Browse the premium food halls of Mitsukoshi and Takashimaya department stores.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the penultimate full day with a world-class omakase dinner at a Michelin-starred restaurant in the Ginza or Nihonbashi area — a full multi-course Japanese tasting menu with wine or sake pairing, representing the pinnacle of Japanese culinary artistry.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — a proper sit-down Japanese morning meal
meals.lunch: Premium tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) at Ginza Bairin or Maisen — a beloved Tokyo institution serving perfectly crispy, juicy premium pork
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred omakase at Saito, Ishikawa, or Kagurazaka Ishikawa — advance reservation essential, booked months ahead

day_by_day.notes: Imperial Palace East Gardens are closed on Mondays and Fridays — verify schedule and adjust day if needed. The Intermediatheque is a hidden gem often overlooked by tourists. Michelin-starred omakase restaurants in Tokyo require reservations made months in advance — book before your trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum in Ryogoku (currently under renovation — confirm status) or alternatively the Sumida Hokusai Museum, dedicated to the legendary ukiyo-e artist Katsushika Hokusai, featuring original woodblock prints, paintings, and interactive digital recreations of his masterworks. Walk across the Kiyosu Bridge over the Sumida River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Attend a sumo stable morning practice (keiko) if available via a specialized cultural tour operator — or visit the Kokugikan Sumo Hall and its sumo museum. Explore the traditional Ryogoku neighborhood, sampling chanko-nabe (the hearty sumo wrestlers' stew) at a local restaurant. Visit the Hamarikyu Gardens again at leisure for a peaceful afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional Japanese onsen and kaiseki dinner at a premium Tokyo ryokan or onsen facility — try Hoshinoya Tokyo (urban ryokan with rooftop onsen) for a uniquely luxurious Japanese inn experience within the city.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or artisan café near Tsukiji
meals.lunch: Chanko-nabe hot pot at a Ryogoku sumo restaurant — a hearty, protein-rich broth stew with vegetables, tofu, and meat, traditionally eaten by sumo wrestlers
meals.dinner: Multi-course kaiseki dinner at Hoshinoya Tokyo or a comparable premium ryokan restaurant — seasonal Japanese cuisine in a serene tatami setting

day_by_day.notes: Confirm Edo-Tokyo Museum reopening status before your trip. Sumo stable visits require advance arrangement through a licensed tour operator and are subject to availability. Hoshinoya Tokyo requires advance reservation and is one of Tokyo's most exclusive urban hospitality experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Kamakura (approximately 1 hour by JR Yokosuka Line from Tokyo Station). Visit the iconic Kotoku-in Temple and its Great Buddha (Daibutsu) — a 13.35-meter bronze statue dating to 1252. Explore the forested Zeniarai Benzaiten Ugafuku Shrine, where visitors wash money in sacred spring water for good fortune.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through bamboo groves and forested hillsides connecting Kamakura's major temples. Visit Engaku-ji and Kencho-ji Zen temples — among Japan's most important Rinzai Zen training monasteries. Browse the artisan shops along Komachi-dori street for handcrafted Japanese goods.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo and enjoy a farewell-eve dinner at a premium restaurant in the Ginza district — perhaps a celebrated French-Japanese fusion restaurant or a legendary sushi counter for one final extraordinary meal.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Kamakura: shirasu (whitebait) rice bowl at a local restaurant — Kamakura's famous local specialty, served raw or cooked over rice with soy sauce
meals.dinner: Premium French-Japanese fusion at Quintessence (Shinagawa) or a celebrated Ginza sushi counter — a memorable final dinner

day_by_day.notes: Kamakura is a popular weekend destination — depart early to beat crowds. The Daibutsu Hiking Trail takes approximately 2 hours at a leisurely pace and involves some uneven terrain. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The JR Pass covers the Yokosuka Line to Kamakura.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the hotel or a final visit to the Tsukiji Outer Market for fresh sushi and tamagoyaki. Pick up any last-minute premium souvenirs: high-grade Japanese teas, artisan ceramics, premium sake, or specialty foods from the market stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time: visit any remaining Tokyo highlights or simply enjoy a relaxed afternoon at a premium café in Ginza or a final stroll along the Sumida River waterfront near your Tsukiji hotel. Check out of your boutique hotel and arrange private transfer to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tokyo. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of food, technology, culture, and unforgettable experiences in one of the world's greatest cities.
